In 1968, one man was introduced to five different classes.
Same man. Same height. A different title each time.
When they thought he was a student, they guessed him shorter.
When they thought he was a professor, he grew over five centimeters.
Height isn't only measured with a tape.
If you've ever felt small in a room, this is for you.
Maybe you stood at the back of every photo.
Maybe you checked who was taller before you sat down.
That feeling is real. And it's not your fault.
Even Napoleon, the famous short emperor, was about average for his time.
People just kept calling him small.
You can't change your height. But you can change how you carry it.
Stand tall. Shoulders back. Head up.
Get strong. Wear clothes that fit you.
Speak slowly. Look people in the eye.
Remember that professor? People see more than centimeters.
Your height is a number. Your presence is a choice.
Tomorrow, walk into one room like you belong there.
